I will keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the safest path for me is still the usual wheat-maize rotation on the same land. I know this system, the buyers know it, the machines fit it, and the weather and irrigation conditions here are better suited to it than taking risks on specialty crops. At the start of the season, my winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, so I will focus first on topdressing, one to two irrigations depending on rain, and disease control if I see pressure from rust, aphids, or scab. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize on the same fields with improved or hybrid seed, keep fertilizer balanced instead of pushing only nitrogen, irrigate mainly at key stages if water is available, and control weeds and corn borers in time. I will use rotary tillage before maize because it is faster and cheaper for me than deep ploughing every season, and it matches how I usually manage labor and cost.
